card.name: Jerkin'
card.tagline: A Los Angeles-born street dance movement defined by rapid legwork and skinny jeans.
card.profile: Jerkin' is a street dance and hip-hop subgenre that originated in the Los Angeles metropolitan area around 2008. Characterized by distinct, rapid leg movements and a rejection of traditional baggy hip-hop attire in favor of skinny jeans and vibrant colors, it gained mainstream prominence through viral YouTube videos and tracks by groups like the New Boyz. While initially rooted in local gang party culture, the dance evolved into a competitive performance art, spreading across the United States and internationally to Europe and Latin America. A 2020s revival has since reimagined the associated 'jerk rap' sound, blending it with contemporary microgenres.
card.insight: Emerging from gang culture as an 'anti-dance' in 2008, Jerkin' transformed into a global performance phenomenon, with crews like The Ranger$ securing major label deals by 2009.

card.profile_long:
Jerkin', also known as 'Jerk', emerged in the Los Angeles metropolitan area around 2008, quickly evolving from a localized party dance into a global street dance phenomenon. According to Oktane of the group Audio Push, the dance originated from gang members at parties who would perform it as an 'anti-dance' to distinguish themselves from others on the floor. By 2009, the movement had gained significant mainstream traction, propelled by the success of the New Boyz's hit 'You're a Jerk' and Audio Push's 'Teach Me How to Jerk'. These tracks, alongside the rise of YouTube as a platform for sharing dance videos, allowed the style to spread rapidly across the United States and into international markets, particularly France and Germany.

The movement is defined by a specific aesthetic that marked a sharp departure from the baggy, oversized clothing traditionally associated with hip-hop culture. Practitioners, known as 'Jerkers', adopted 'swag' fashion, which features skinny jeans, bright-colored clothing, novelty graphic tees, and retro high-top sneakers such as Chuck Taylors, Nikes, Supras, or Vlado footwear. This fashion choice was a deliberate rejection of the baggy pants style, emphasizing a leaner, more colorful silhouette that aligned with the high-energy, rapid-fire nature of the dance steps.

The dance itself is characterized by intricate footwork and specific, named movements. The core 'jerk' motion involves moving the legs in and out, often accompanied by the 'reject' (a backward leg rotation), the 'dip' (small steps followed by a sudden stop), and the 'pindrop' (a rapid rotation of the leg below the knee). As the style evolved, it incorporated influences from other dance forms, including the Melbourne Shuffle, leading to more complex footwork sequences. In the early 2020s, the movement experienced a resurgence through a new generation of underground rappers and producers, such as Xaviersobased and his collective 1c34, who reimagined the original 'jerk rap' sound with faster tempos and contemporary electronic influences.

Throughout its history, Jerkin' has functioned as both a social activity and a competitive performance art. Dance crews like The Ranger$, Marvel Inc., and the U.C.L.A. Jerk Kings became central figures, competing in events and recording their own music. The culture remains a living tradition, with its influence extending into modern microgenres and continuing to evolve through digital platforms where new steps and trends are shared by practitioners worldwide.

sections.origins_and_history: Jerkin' originated in Los Angeles in 2008, initially as a dance performed by gang members at parties. It gained widespread popularity in 2009 through the music of the New Boyz and Audio Push, eventually spreading across the US and internationally.
sections.how_it_is_danced: The dance is defined by detailed footwork. Key moves include the 'jerk' (moving legs in and out), the 'reject' (backward leg rotation), the 'dip' (steps followed by a block), and the 'pindrop' (rapid leg rotation below the knee).
sections.music_and_instruments: The music, known as 'jerk rap', is characterized by upbeat, dance-oriented hip-hop. In the 2020s, the sound evolved to include faster tempos, melodic synth layers, and abstract, off-kilter lyrics.
sections.costume_and_setting: Practitioners wear skinny jeans, bright-colored clothing, graphic tees, and retro high-top sneakers. This style is a rejection of traditional baggy hip-hop clothing.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: Originally an 'anti-dance' within gang culture, it transitioned into a competitive performance style showcased at events and on YouTube. It is a social dance often performed in crews.
sections.notable_figures: New Boyz, Audio Push, The Ranger$, Rej3ctz, Xaviersobased, and the 1c34 collective.
sections.regional_variants: The dance spread from the US West Coast to the East Coast, France, Germany, and Latin American countries like the Dominican Republic and Panama.
sections.lineage: A subgenre of hip-hop and street dance, with later influences from cloud rap, plugg music, and digicore.

steps.name: Advanced Reject
steps.description: A normal reject where you twist your foot inwards on your toes.

steps.name: Melbourne Shuffle
steps.description: Pick your non-dominant foot, make a twist on your heel, then toe, heel, toe.

steps.name: Heel-Toe
steps.description: Carve the heel by twisting in and out with one foot while swinging the other foot up and down.

steps.name: Heel-Toe Step
steps.description: Carve with your heel again, then carve with your toe right after, followed by a step.

steps.name: Criss-Cross
steps.description: Keep feet separated, put them together, then separate them and cross the opposite way.

steps.name: Steez Step
steps.description: Turn to one side, then jump to the other side.
